database_summary: E-commerce dataset with customers, sellers, products, orders and related events (items, payments, reviews) plus geolocation lookup and a small leads CRM (qualified and closed). Mix of current-state descriptive tables (products, sellers, customers), event/history tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews, leads_closed), and lookup/dimension tables (product_category_name_translation, geolocation). Row counts range from hundreds to ~1M for geolocation; common keys are order_id, product_id, seller_id, customer_id, and zip-code prefixes.

accepted.name: orders_enriched_with_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
accepted.description: One row per order enriched with customer demographic fields (join orders -> customers). Useful as a starting point for analyses that need order timestamps, status and customer location or to join further to order-level facts like payments or reviews. | Use for: orders by customer location or state; time-to-delivery analyses per customer cohort; order counts or funnels by customer demographic groups

accepted.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  oi.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value
FROM order_items oi
LEFT JOIN products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN sellers s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
accepted.description: One row per order item enriched with product attributes and seller location fields. Useful for product-level revenue, size/weight analyses, seller performance, or joining to orders/payments/reviews. | Use for: item-level revenue or margin analyses; delivery / shipping SLA by product or seller; product size/weight impact on freight

accepted.name: order_payments_agg_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_rows_count,
  AVG(payment_installments) AS avg_payment_installments
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: One row per order summarizing payment measures (total paid, number of payment methods, majority payment_type not exposed). Useful for order-level revenue, average payment installments, and to detect multi-payment orders. | Use for: order revenue / reconciliation checks; payment behavior analyses (installments, multiple payments); filtering orders by total paid

accepted.name: order_reviews_with_order_dates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date
FROM order_reviews r
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON r.order_id = o.order_id
accepted.description: One row per review enriched with the order's purchase and delivery timestamps. Useful to analyze review scores relative to delivery times or purchase date. | Use for: impact of delivery speed on review_score; time between purchase and review; textual review analysis with order context

accepted.name: customer_latest_order_date
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp AS latest_order_purchase_timestamp
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders o
) WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: One row per customer_id with their latest order_purchase_timestamp. Useful to determine recency, active customers, or to join as a latest-order snapshot for churn/retention cohorts. | Use for: RFM / recency calculations; identify active vs lapsed customers; join most recent order attributes to customer profile

accepted.name: geolocation_latest_per_zip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat,
  geolocation_lng,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_state
FROM (
  SELECT
    g.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ORDER BY g.geolocation_lat DESC, g.geolocation_lng DESC) AS rn
  FROM geolocation g
) WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: One representative geolocation row per geolocation_zip_code_prefix selecting the latest/last coordinate by latitude+longitude textual sort. Because geolocation may have multiple coordinates per prefix, this provides a deterministic single-row-per-zip for map joins. Use when a single lat/lng per zip is needed. | Use for: map visualizations by zip; join customers/sellers to a single lat/lng per zip; distance / proximity calculations using a canonical coordinate per zip

accepted.name: product_category_translation
accepted.description: One row per product_category_name providing the English translation. Useful to standardize category names for reporting or to join to products to expose an English-friendly category label. | Use for: translate product categories for dashboards; grouping products by English category labels

accepted.name: products_with_standard_dimensions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) AS volume_cm3
FROM products
accepted.description: One row per product_id with size and weight columns preserved and an additional derived volume_cm3. Useful for analyzing shipping costs, volumetric sizing, and product physical characteristics. | Use for: shipping cost estimation by volume/weight; product physical attributes summaries; filter products by size thresholds

accepted.name: orders_with_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  COALESCE(oi.items_total_price, 0) AS items_total_price,
  COALESCE(oi.items_total_freight, 0) AS items_total_freight,
  COALESCE(op.total_payment_value, 0) AS total_payment_value,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    SUM(price) AS items_total_price,
    SUM(freight_value) AS items_total_freight
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) op ON o.order_id = op.order_id
accepted.description: One row per order combining order-level payments aggregates and item-level totals (sum price and freight) by joining aggregated order_items and order_payments. Useful for order reconciliation and per-order revenue metrics. | Use for: order-level revenue reconciliation; detect undervalued or unpaid orders; compare item totals to payment totals
